rationale: Across all reporting cohorts, PLAA-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (NDMSBA; OMIM #617527) manifests with early infantile onset (typically 2-4 months of age) characterized by progressive (postnatal) microcephaly, spastic quadriparesis, leukoencephalopathy, epileptic encephalopathy, and profound developmental regression/delay. This presentation clearly contrasts with autosomal recessive primary microcephaly (MCPH), which characteristically presents with static congenital microcephaly and non-progressive intellectual disability without early severe white matter degeneration or rapid neurological decline.

evidence.text: Seven patients from an initial cohort presented at ages 2 to 4 months with progressive microcephaly, spastic quadriparesis, global developmental delay, and severe leukoencephalopathy associated with homozygous loss-of-function variants in PLAA (p.Leu752Phe).

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic frequency of optic atrophy and retinal degeneration across all published PLAA-deficient cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: While progressive microcephaly, spasticity, and leukoencephalopathy are well documented across cohorts, systematic ophthalmologic profiling has not been aggregated with standardized denominators.

new_directions.question_text: Does residual PLAA function correlate with survival into later childhood versus early infantile lethality?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether hypomorphic missense variants cause non-lethal atypical cerebral palsy phenotypes compared to null variants can refine genotype-phenotype differentiation.
